findings.evidence: Line 416 is `rfl` directly after the `rw` at line 415. The function `f` is built with `continuousLinearMap_comp (ContinuousLinearMap.apply ℝ ℝ (finBasis ℝ F c))`, while the lower bound `hC` states the same quantity as a pointwise lambda.
findings.fix: Close the goal with an explicit rewrite such as `simp [ContinuousLinearMap.sub_apply]` or `congr 2; funext z; simp`, or add a comment explaining why the definitional equality holds.
findings.issue: In `he`, after `rw [Pi.sub_apply, ← MemLp.toLp_sub, Lp.norm_toLp]` the goal is closed by a bare `rfl`. This only works because unfolding `ContinuousLinearMap.apply`, `Pi.sub` and continuous-linear-map subtraction happens to identify `fun z ↦ (θ Λ i z - θ Λ' i z) (b c)` with the difference of the composed functions. No comment explains this.

findings.evidence: grep: line 242 `((show (Q₀ : Set ℂ) ⊆ Q from hQ₀).trans hQ') hw`; line 255 `Measure.restrict_mono ((show (Q₀ : Set ℂ) ⊆ Q from hQ₀).trans`.
findings.fix: Name the fact once with an explicit lemma, e.g. `have hQ₀' : (Q₀ : Set ℂ) ⊆ Q := SetLike.coe_subset_coe.2 hQ₀`, and use `hQ₀'` at both places.
findings.issue: `show (Q₀ : Set ℂ) ⊆ Q from hQ₀` converts the `Opens` order to set inclusion by definitional equality, with no comment. The same cast is repeated at line 255.

findings.evidence: Lines 325-330: the `show` repeats the right-hand side of the calc step at lines 319-320 word for word.
findings.fix: Write the previous calc line directly in the form `k i * ((∑ c, e i c) * ‖w‖)`, or close this step with `calc _ = k i * _ := by rw [hk]; ring` followed by `gcongr`, so the expression is not repeated by hand.
findings.issue: `rw [show (Kb * ∑ c, e i c) * (‖…chartValueL…‖ * (‖P i‖ * ‖w‖)) = k i * … by rw [hk]; ring]` copies out the whole goal term to rearrange it. This breaks whenever the previous calc step changes shape.

summary: The proofs are well organised and short enough, but one closing `rfl` and several uncommented `show` steps rely on definitional equality that a rename or refactor would break.
